title: Owner Auto Policy Claims–Underwriting Liaison Note — Effective Date When a Resident Is Listed Again
content:
**Rule.** When a household resident is listed again as a rated driver on the Owner Auto Policy, the days charged run from the listing effective date to the expiration date. This covers a resident who was reported, on a claim of the term under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), operating a scheduled vehicle while an unlisted household resident.

The listing effective date is read from:
- the resident's most recent entry on the term;
- the report date and reported date of loss of that claim report.

| Resident's most recent entry on the term | Listing |
|---|---|
| A driver-removed entry dated before the report date | takes effect on the later of the report date (the day the company learned the resident was again operating a scheduled vehicle) and the day after the reported date of loss; days charged run from it to expiration |
| A driver-added entry dated after the reported date of loss | the resident is already listed again, and nothing is charged (no days) |
| Otherwise | takes effect on the later of the processing date and the day after the reported date of loss; days charged run from it to expiration |

The listing effective date is counted and the expiration date is not.

The listing never takes effect on or before the date of loss. So the coverage decision on that loss still reads the resident as unlisted.

**Hypothetical cases.**
- The resident was removed on the 1st, the claim was reported on the 12th and the loss was on the 10th. The listing takes effect on the 12th.
- Same facts, but reported on the 10th, the day of the loss. The listing takes effect on the 11th.
- The resident's latest entry is a driver-added entry dated the 15th, after a loss on the 10th. Nothing is charged.
